title: footgun: config.maxSubSteps (schema-capped at 16) reads as the ceiling on physics substeps per tick.
detail: It is combined via Math.max(configMax, min(requiredSteps,48)) then subSteps=min(requiredSteps,effectiveLimit), which algebraically reduces to subSteps=min(requiredSteps,48) for every input. maxSubSteps never changes the substep count; the real (and only) cap is the hardcoded ABSOLUTE_MAX_SUBSTEPS=48.

title: footgun: ImpulseConfig exposes a user-facing subSteps slider described 'Physics sub-steps per frame' (impulseConfig schema, default 1), implying it controls the tick substep count.
detail: tick() derives subSteps purely from dt (requiredSteps) and the 48-cap; config.subSteps is never read here or anywhere in src, so the slider has no effect on the simulation.

title: footgun: computeObstacleAvoidance takes a general 'neighbors' list and is fed the full spatial query buffer, reading as if it avoids all nearby bodies.
detail: 'if (!neighbor.isStatic) continue;' skips every dynamic body, so only STATIC bodies are ever treated as obstacles; dynamic bodies are never avoided by this path (they rely on separation instead).

title: footgun: queryRadius is documented as returning 'all bodies that *might* collide with the given circle (x, y, radius)'.
detail: It queries a square (half-extent=radius, not a circle) and its containment test only checks each neighbor's CENTER against that box, ignoring the neighbor's own radius, so a large body straddling the query circle from just outside can be missed; it is not collision-complete.

title: footgun: applySeek is exported as part of the steering API, implying it is a live force applied during ticks.
detail: applySeek has zero callers anywhere in src (only computeSeek is used); it is dead exported code.

title: footgun: applySeparation is exported alongside computeSeparation and takes a Quadtree, implying it is the live separation entry point.
detail: applySeparation has zero callers in src; the live path is computeSeparation via ImpulseSteeringForces, and this quadtree-based wrapper is dead code.

title: clampToBounds replaces the position object instead of mutating in place
detail: Every other code path mutates body.position.x/y in place, but clampToBounds reassigns body.position to a fresh {x,y}. Any code holding a reference to the previous position Vector2 (renderer, cached alias) silently keeps the stale, unclamped object and diverges from the body.

title: Coincident bodies always separate along +X only
detail: When two bodies are within 0.0001 the code does 'dx += 1; distance = 1;' but never adjusts dy, so exactly-stacked bodies are always pushed apart along +X. Perfectly-overlapping clusters fan out on one axis, producing a directional bias rather than isotropic dispersal.

title: Shared mutable zeroVector singleton returned to callers
detail: computeWobbleForce (and the zeroVector singletons in ImpulseSteeringHelpers.ts:7 and ImpulseAnchor.ts:4) return one shared {x:0,y:0} object. Current callers only read it, but any future consumer that mutates a returned force vector in place would corrupt the global zero for all subsequent callers this frame.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real: setWorldBounds silently returns (no-op) when width/height are non-finite or below config.minWorldSize, giving the caller no signal. A caller that passes a too-small or NaN size believes bounds were set while the engine keeps its previous/null bounds, leaving the simulation effectively unbounded (clampToBounds becomes a no-op).

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Mostly benign: setTarget returns silently when bodyId is not in the map, so a mistimed setTarget for a not-yet-added or already-removed body is dropped with no error or return value; the seek simply never engages and the failure is untraced.
